newsitem.title: USA: Netrix to drop Internet access mkt efforts.
newsitem.headline: Netrix to drop Internet access mkt efforts.

text.p: Netrix Corp Wednesday said it will intensify its business focus on the enterprise network market and discontinue initiatives into the Internet access market, including its initial product the micro.pop 2300 system announced in early 1996.

Netrix said it will focus on applications for both its Frame Access Node 2210 and the new multi-service Network Exchange 2550. These applications include voice, data, and fax over frame relay, and the transition of legacy data networks from SNA and X.25 to frame relay and ATM in hybrid public/private frame relay networks.

"Since introducing the 2210 a year ago, we have seen sales increase every quarter. The opportunity for voice and data networking over Frame Relay, on a world-wide basis, is growing rapidly, and we want to apply our efforts to that market," said Lynn Chapman, president and chief executive.

Chapman added, "The micro.pop required that we establish a different distribution channel and make substantial ongoing R&D investments. Although the Internet access market opportunity is large, we do not want to dilute our efforts, capital or focus given the prospects for significant growth for our 2210 and 2550 product family."
Netrix manufactures and markets products for enterprise networks and public network access.
